articles.title: Why Composable CDPs Break Without Strict Ingestion Data Contracts
articles.excerpt: The promise of the composable Customer Data Platform (CDP), is intoxicating to any leader tired of vendor lock-in. Instead of shipping your first-party data to a proprietary cloud silo, you leave it i…
articles.body: The promise of the composable Customer Data Platform (CDP), is intoxicating to any leader tired of vendor lock-in. Instead of shipping your first-party data to a proprietary cloud silo, you leave it in your own warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks), and "activate" it using lightweight tools. It is a strategy of architectural liberation. But for many enterprises, this dream of agility quickly dissolves into a nightmare of broken pipelines and erratic customer segments. The culprit is rarely the activation tool itself. The failure usually lives at the point of ingestion. When you move from a monolithic CDP to a composable one, you lose the vendor’s rigid, pre-defined schema.

articles.body: Today we’re excited to release VEKTOR v2.0.9. We have built a Humanizer tool to reformat and improve machine-like writing, an AI-text detector tool to check if writing is made by an LLM, and improvements to our Faraday security module benchmarks. How does a small AI detector tell machine text from human text? You paste a draft into the document detector, and it will provide a readout. You get a likelihood in plain words and the text-colored sentence by sentence. Nothing leaves your computer. We tried the zero-shot methods first (Binoculars with SmolLM2–360M, Fast-DetectGPT). On our RAID sample Binoculars scored 0.81 AUROC and caught 54% of machine text at a 5% false-alarm line. It also needs two language models (about 726 MB) and takes about a second per text.

articles.title: 8 queens: 16.7 million boards, or 2,056 placements
articles.excerpt: Suppose you're asked to place n queens on an n × n board so that none of them attacks another. I'd guess most people's first program picks n squares out of the n² available and then checks whether the…
articles.body: Suppose you're asked to place n queens on an n × n board so that none of them attacks another. I'd guess most people's first program picks n squares out of the n² available and then checks whether the result works. You can improve that slightly, because two queens in the same row always attack each other, so you'd pick one column for each row and check afterwards. However, both versions build complete boards before judging them. Backtracking checks each queen at the moment it's placed and abandons a board as soon as it's clear it can't work. n Any n squares One per row, then check Queens placed by backtracking Solutions 4 1,820 256 16 2 6 1,947,792 46,656 152 4 8 4,426,165,368 16,777,216 2,056 92 You'll notice the difference isn't a constant factor.

articles.title: How an AI Voice Detector Works: Features, Classifiers and a Toy Python Example
articles.excerpt: By Tania Alwan Cloned and synthetic voices are now easy to make, so "is this voice real?" has become a practical question for podcasters, journalists, call centres and musicians. An AI voice detector…
articles.body: By Tania Alwan Cloned and synthetic voices are now easy to make, so "is this voice real?" has become a practical question for podcasters, journalists, call centres and musicians. An AI voice detector tries to answer it automatically. This post explains how these detectors work under the hood, what the research community uses to test them, where they fail, and then builds a deliberately tiny detector in Python so you can see the moving parts. Spoiler: the toy works on toy data. Real detection is much harder, and I will be explicit about why. What an AI voice detector is actually trying to do In research, this problem is usually called spoofing detection or anti-spoofing , and the detector is a countermeasure (CM) .

articles.title: Azure DevOps Crash Course (Part 5): Deploy to Azure App Service with Dev, Prod and Approvals
articles.excerpt: I still remember my first "real" deployment. It was a Friday (I know, I never learn), and it involved copying files over remote desktop, editing a config file by hand, and praying. When something brok…
articles.body: I still remember my first "real" deployment. It was a Friday (I know, I never learn), and it involved copying files over remote desktop, editing a config file by hand, and praying. When something broke, nobody knew which version was running. A deployment pipeline fixes all of that. Same steps every time, a clear history of what went where, and a human approval before anything touches production. In Part 4 our pipeline learned to build and test the Todo API. Today we teach it to deploy : first to a Dev environment automatically, then to Prod after someone clicks Approve . What you need to know before the code A pipeline can have stages . Think of them as chapters: Build, then Dev, then Prod. We build once and save the result as a zip file (an artifact ). Dev and Prod deploy that same zip.

articles.excerpt: Fewer hardware launches could mean more time for meaningful upgrades.
articles.body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly plans to skip new Galaxy Watch models in 2027, breaking its annual release tradition. The move to a two-year launch cycle aims to reduce development and marketing costs. Samsung plans to focus on software updates and new health features for existing Galaxy Watches. Not every smartwatch needs a new model every year. Apple demonstrated that when it waited two years between the Watch Ultra 2 and Ultra 3, releasing only a new color in between. And with yearly hardware improvements becoming increasingly modest, there’s a growing debate over whether annual upgrades are still necessary. Samsung could now take things a step further by abandoning yearly Galaxy Watch releases altogether.

The first 20 or so hours I’ve spent with Rockstar’s triumphant return to Vice City have transported me to an impossibly high fidelity game world and treated me to criminal capers so immaculately crafted they make Michael Mann seem more like a Michael mouse. As I’ve made my way across the sprawling Leonida map I’ve relished each and every unethical exploit of lawbreaking lovebirds, Jason and Lucia. So far I’ve been Jason the wheelman, Jason the bagman, and Jason the hitman, but to my surprise, what I really want to be is… Tim the Toolman? Before you hit me with one of Tim Allen’s trademark quizzical caveman grunts, let me back up for a moment.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX just launched two rockets from the same California pad 32 hours apart, breaking its own turnaround record by about 13 hours.
articles.body: SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!
